definition: Small data files created and stored by the website you're directly visiting to remember information about your visit and preferences on that specific site.
metaDescription: Learn about first party cookies - data files created by websites you visit to remember your preferences and improve your browsing experience.
simpleExplanation: Think of first party cookies as a website's memory about you. When you visit a site, it creates these small files on your device to remember things like your login status, items in your shopping cart, or language preferences.
whyItMatters: First party cookies are generally considered privacy-friendly because they only work on the site that created them. They improve your browsing experience by keeping you logged in and remembering your preferences without sharing data with other websites.
technicalDetail: First party cookies are set by the domain in your browser's address bar and can only be read by that same domain. They're stored locally on your device and sent back to the originating server with each request, enabling stateful interactions in the otherwise stateless HTTP protocol.

examples.explanation: When you add items to your cart on an e-commerce site, a first party cookie remembers those items so they're still there when you return to the site later.
After logging into your email account, a first party cookie keeps you signed in so you don't have to enter your password every time you check a new message.
A news website uses first party cookies to remember that you prefer dark mode and want articles displayed in large text, applying these settings each time you visit.
